donuts.name: Classic Glazed

ingredients: Glaze: 2 cups powdered sugar, 3–4 tbsp milk, 1 tsp vanilla
steps: Bloom yeast in warm milk with a pinch of sugar until foamy.
Mix in sugar, eggs, butter, flour, and salt; knead until smooth and soft.
Rise until doubled, roll to ½ inch, cut rings, and rise again.
Fry at 350°F until golden; drain on a rack.
Dip warm donuts in vanilla glaze and let them shine.

donuts.history: Yeast-raised rings with a thin sugar glaze became an American bakery staple in the early 20th century, riding the rise of doughnut shops and chain counters. The glaze isn’t just sweet — it seals in moisture so the pillowy crumb stays soft for hours.
donuts.avatarScript: Classic Glazed is the handshake of the donut world — yeast dough, hot oil, and a glassy vanilla coat.

donuts.name: Boston Cream

ingredients: 1 batch yeast donut dough (see Classic Glazed)
Custard: 2 cups milk, ½ cup sugar, 4 yolks, 3 tbsp cornstarch, 1 tsp vanilla, 2 tbsp butter
Chocolate ganache: 6 oz dark chocolate, ½ cup warm cream
steps: Fry round yeast donuts until deep golden; cool.
Cook custard until thick; chill until pipeable.
Poke a hole and pipe in custard.
Dip tops in glossy chocolate ganache.

donuts.history: Boston cream donuts borrow the spirit of Boston cream pie — sponge, custard, and chocolate turned into a portable filled treat.
donuts.avatarScript: Boston Cream is dessert cosplay: vanilla custard inside, chocolate on top.

donuts.name: Raspberry Jelly

steps: Fry round donuts; cool slightly.
Warm jam and pipe into the center.
Dust generously in powdered sugar.

donuts.history: Jelly-filled doughnuts travel with Central and Eastern European traditions into North American bakeries — raspberry cuts through fried dough with bright acid.
donuts.avatarScript: Raspberry Jelly is the plot twist donut — quiet powdered exterior, then a berry burst.

donuts.name: Old-Fashioned

steps: Cream butter and sugar; beat in yolks and sour cream.
Fold in dry ingredients; chill briefly.
Cut rings and fry until deeply golden with cracked edges.
Dip in thin glaze so it pools in every crevice.

donuts.history: Old-fashioned cake donuts lean on sour cream for tenderness and signature cracks — denser than yeast rings, built to catch glaze.
donuts.avatarScript: Old-Fashioned is the crunchy-edged cousin — cake crumb, nutmeg hush, glaze in every crack.

donuts.name: Maple Walnut

ingredients: Maple glaze: 1½ cups powdered sugar, 3 tbsp maple syrup, 1–2 tbsp milk, pinch salt
steps: Fry and cool donuts until just warm.
Whisk maple glaze until thick but pourable.
Dip tops, then press on toasted walnuts.

donuts.history: Maple syrup has deep roots in Indigenous North American foodways and New England sugarhouses — bakery maple glazes turned that sweetness into a cold-weather favorite.
donuts.avatarScript: Maple Walnut tastes like autumn trees — sticky maple shine and walnut crunch.

donuts.name: French Cruller

steps: Make choux paste; beat in eggs one at a time.
Pipe rings with a star tip.
Fry until puffed, hollow, and golden.
Glaze lightly so the ridges stay visible.

donuts.history: French crullers use pâte à choux — the same airy dough behind éclairs — piped into ridged rings and fried.
donuts.avatarScript: French Cruller is the ballerina of the case — choux dough and a glaze that almost floats.

donuts.name: Chocolate Frosted

ingredients: Chocolate frosting: 2 cups powdered sugar, ⅓ cup cocoa, 3–4 tbsp milk, 1 tsp vanilla
steps: Fry and cool donuts.
Whisk frosting until thick and glossy.
Dip tops and shower with sprinkles before it sets.

donuts.history: Chocolate-frosted rings with sprinkles became the kid-counter favorite mid-century — cocoa frosting sticks better than thin glaze for holding candy colors.
donuts.avatarScript: Chocolate Frosted is pure celebration energy — cocoa hat and a confetti of sprinkles.

donuts.name: Strawberry Sprinkle

ingredients: Strawberry frosting: 2 cups powdered sugar, 2–3 tbsp strawberry puree or jam, splash of milk
steps: Fry and cool donuts.
Beat frosting until smooth and bright pink.
Dip and decorate with sprinkles.

donuts.history: Strawberry frosting rode the wave of mid-century soda-fountain colors — bright pink became a bakery shorthand for fun long before Instagram.
donuts.avatarScript: Strawberry Sprinkle is Glazed’s pink wink — berry frost and a sparkle of candy.

donuts.name: Lemon Poppy

ingredients: Lemon glaze: 1½ cups powdered sugar, 2–3 tbsp lemon juice, zest of 1 lemon
steps: Fry or bake donuts; cool slightly.
Whisk lemon glaze; stir in most of the poppy seeds.
Dip and finish with a pinch more seeds and zest.

donuts.history: Lemon-poppy is a muffin classic that jumped the counter — citrus cuts richness, and poppy seeds add a delicate crunch without heavy topping.
donuts.avatarScript: Lemon Poppy wakes up the case — sunshine glaze and tiny seed crackle.

donuts.name: Apple Fritter

steps: Toss apples with dry ingredients; fold in milk and egg.
Scoop irregular mounds into 350°F oil.
Fry until deep golden; glaze while warm.

donuts.history: Fritters are older than the ring donut — fruit batter fried in oil shows up across many cultures. Apple fritters became a U.S. bakery staple for fall mornings.
donuts.avatarScript: Apple Fritter breaks the ring rule — crispy edges, soft apple pockets, sticky glaze.

donuts.name: Cinnamon Sugar

steps: Fry cake donuts until golden.
Toss warm donuts in cinnamon sugar (butter helps it cling).
Serve while still fragrant.

donuts.history: Cinnamon sugar is the simplest finish — spice and crystals instead of glaze — beloved for coffee-shop mornings and kid counters alike.
donuts.avatarScript: Cinnamon Sugar is cozy minimalism — warm spice that sticks to your fingers.

donuts.name: Matcha White Chocolate

ingredients: Matcha glaze: 1½ cups powdered sugar, 1–1½ tsp culinary matcha, 2–3 tbsp milk
2 oz melted white chocolate for drizzle
steps: Fry and cool donuts.
Whisk matcha glaze until smooth and vivid.
Dip tops, then zigzag white chocolate.

donuts.history: Matcha moved from tea ceremony into pastry cases worldwide in the 2010s — paired with white chocolate it balances bitter green notes with creamy sweetness.
donuts.avatarScript: Matcha White Chocolate is the modern looker — jade glaze with a sweet white drizzle.

donuts.name: Blueberry Cake

ingredients: Glaze: 1½ cups powdered sugar, 2–3 tbsp blueberry puree or milk, splash of lemon
steps: Whisk dry ingredients; fold in buttermilk, eggs, and butter.
Gently fold blueberries — don’t crush them.
Pipe or spoon into a donut pan (or fry cake rings at 365°F).
Bake at 375°F about 12 minutes, or fry until deep golden.
Cool slightly, then dip in blueberry glaze.

donuts.history: A baker’s dozen means the lucky extra — once a goodwill cushion so customers never got shorted by weight. Blueberry cake donuts carry that counter-culture spirit: dense, fruity, and the one that rounds out the box.
donuts.avatarScript: Blueberry Cake is the baker’s dozen lucky extra — purple-kissed cake crumb.

smoothies.name: Mango Sunrise

ingredients: ¾ cup orange juice or coconut milk
steps: Blend until silky.
Add liquid to reach a thick sip.
Pour cold and serve with a straw.

smoothies.history: Mango smoothies rode the 1990s–2000s juice-bar boom — ripe mango’s natural sweetness needs little sugar, so the drink stays bright and thick.
smoothies.avatarScript: Mango Sunrise is liquid sunshine — thick gold you can drink beside a warm donut.

smoothies.name: Berry Blast

ingredients: ¾ cup apple juice or milk
steps: Blend until smooth and vivid purple-red.
Taste for tartness; sweeten lightly if needed.
Serve immediately.

smoothies.history: Berry blends became smoothie-bar staples for color and punchy flavor — a tart counterpoint to sweet bakery cases.
smoothies.avatarScript: Berry Blast is the bold cup — deep berry color that wakes up the counter.

smoothies.name: Tropical Green

steps: Blend spinach with liquid first.
Add fruit and blend until bright green.
Serve cold.

smoothies.history: Green smoothies popularized veggies-in-a-cup in the 2010s — pineapple and banana keep spinach friendly for first-timers.
smoothies.avatarScript: Tropical Green is the sneaky healthy one — paradise flavor with a leafy wink.

smoothies.name: Strawberry Banana

steps: Blend until creamy pink.
Adjust thickness with milk.
Pour and garnish with a berry if you like.

smoothies.history: Strawberry-banana is the gateway smoothie — soft fruit, familiar sweetness, and the drink most people order first at a donut-and-smoothie counter.
smoothies.avatarScript: Strawberry Banana is the classic handshake of the smoothie board — pink, creamy, forever.

smoothies.name: Cookies & Cream

ingredients: 2 cups vanilla ice cream or frozen yogurt
steps: Blend milk, ice cream, and vanilla until smooth.
Pulse in cookies so you still get crunchy bits.
Pour and top with cookie crumbs.

smoothies.history: Cookies-and-cream jumped from ice cream aisles into blender bars — a dessert cup that fits right beside a glazed donut case.
smoothies.avatarScript: Cookies & Cream is the dessert twin of the board — creamy, cookie-crunch, zero regrets.

smoothies.name: PB Banana Cocoa
smoothies.tagline: Peanut butter hug in a cup

steps: Blend until thick and silky.
Taste for sweetness; add honey if needed.
Serve with a peanut-butter swirl if you’re feeling fancy.

smoothies.history: Peanut butter–banana drinks grew up in home kitchens and gyms, then landed on smoothie boards as the filling, savory-sweet option next to fruit cups.
smoothies.avatarScript: PB Banana Cocoa is the power hug — nutty, chocolatey, and perfect after a maple donut.
